```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.2, dpi = 96)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(EpiTracer))
```

`call_simple_excision()` ([its vignette](calling.html)) works from PURPLE/GRIDSS
copy-number and structural-variant calls. `call_episomal_from_ampliconsuite()`
applies the **same episome model** directly to
[AmpliconSuite](https://github.com/AmpliconSuite) output —
[AmpliconArchitect](https://github.com/AmpliconSuite/AmpliconArchitect) (AA) plus
[AmpliconClassifier](https://github.com/AmpliconSuite/AmpliconClassifier) (AC) —
so ecDNA calls from community resources such as
[AmpliconRepository](https://ampliconrepository.org) can be classified as
episomal (simple-excision circle) or not, unified with the PURPLE-native engine.

It is a **self-contained module** (it does not touch `call_simple_excision()`),
built around three exported functions:

| function | role |
|---|---|
| `read_ampliconsuite()` | parse an AA `*_graph.txt` into copy-number segments + SV junctions |
| `aa_cycle_intervals()` | derive the ecDNA extent from an AA `*_cycles.txt` when there is no AC BED |
| `call_episomal_from_ampliconsuite()` | classify one AC ecDNA feature as episomal / bridged / complex |

## Inputs

Two files per amplicon, both standard AmpliconSuite output:

- an AmpliconArchitect **`*_graph.txt`** — `sequence` edges are copy-number
  segments (column 4 = `PredictedCopyCount`), `discordant` edges are SV junctions
  (column 3 = junction copy number, column 4 = `NumberOfReadPairs`, i.e. the
  read-pair support the caller uses);
- the AmpliconClassifier ecDNA interval BED
  **`*_amplicon<N>_ecDNA_<k>_intervals.bed`**, which defines the **amplicon
  extent** — AA/AC's own call, so no copy-number threshold is re-applied here.

## Two gold standards

The package bundles the AmpliconSuite output for two well-characterised ecDNA
cell lines (from AmpliconRepository; cell-line data, no patient data):

- **GBM39** — an *EGFR* ecDNA that is a **simple-excision circle** (episomal);
- **COLO320DM** — the canonical *MYC* ecDNA, which is **complex**, not a simple
  excision.

```{r fixtures}
aa <- function(f) system.file("extdata", "ampliconsuite", f, package = "EpiTracer")

gbm39_graph <- aa("GBM39_EGFR_graph.txt")
gbm39_bed   <- aa("GBM39_EGFR_ecDNA_1_intervals.bed")
colo_graph  <- aa("COLO320DM_MYC_graph.txt")
colo_bed    <- aa("COLO320DM_MYC_ecDNA_1_intervals.bed")
```

`read_ampliconsuite()` parses the graph. AA writes each junction in an arbitrary
orientation, so the SV class is assigned **after sorting the two breakends by
coordinate** (`lo`/`hi`): a `lo-`/`hi+` pair is a head-to-tail duplication — the
circulariser. In GBM39 the highest read-pair-support DUP brackets the EGFR
amplicon — the boundary DUP:

```{r read}
gr <- read_ampliconsuite(gbm39_graph)
gr$junctions[order(-pe_support),
             c("cA", "pA", "cB", "pB", "svclass", "jcn", "pe_support")]
```

## Classifying the two amplicons

```{r call}
gbm39 <- call_episomal_from_ampliconsuite(gbm39_graph, gbm39_bed)
colo  <- call_episomal_from_ampliconsuite(colo_graph,  colo_bed)

cols <- c("status", "episomal", "chimeric", "n_chr",
          "bd_chr", "bd_pe_support", "bd_occupancy", "n_junctions")
cbind(cell_line = c("GBM39", "COLO320DM"), rbind(gbm39, colo)[, cols, with = FALSE])
```

**GBM39** is `episomal` — a boundary DUP brackets the EGFR extent, which is fully
amplified (`bd_occupancy ≈ 1`). **COLO320DM** is `complex`: its 25 amplicon
junctions contain no single DUP that brackets the MYC ecDNA extent, so there is
no boundary DUP (`bd_chr = NA`) — the discrimination the caller is built for.

## The episome model

An amplicon is **episomal** when a **boundary DUP** exists:

1. **Extent** comes from AmpliconSuite itself (the AC ecDNA interval BED, or the
   dominant AA cycle) — no copy-number cutoff is applied here.
2. **Boundary DUP** = an intra-chromosomal duplication whose two ends *bracket*
   the ecDNA's outer boundary on its chromosome (`lo ≤ extent start` and
   `hi ≥ extent end`).
3. **Episomal** if ≥ 1 boundary DUP exists. The boundary DUP reported is the one
   with the **highest read-pair support** *among the spanning DUPs* — a selector,
   not a gate: a higher-support DEL or INV elsewhere in the amplicon does **not**
   veto the call.
4. **Chimeric episomal** — a multi-chromosome ecDNA where *every* chromosome is
   bracketed by its own boundary DUP **and** at least one translocation joins
   them (two episomes fused into one circle).
5. **Internal structure is ignored** — an episome may be heavily rearranged
   internally (chromothripsis within a micronucleus); only the circularising
   boundary matters, never the junction count.

Two guards reject amplicons that pass the geometry but are not self-contained
circles:

- **Occupancy guard** (`min_occupancy`, default `0.05`) — the boundary-DUP
  bracketed span must be > 5 % covered by the ecDNA intervals. A lone DUP
  spanning a largely diploid region (e.g. across a whole chromosome arm) is not a
  circle. The default was calibrated on a PCAWG-vs-PURPLE concordance sweep.
- **Bridged / ambiguous downgrade** (`bridge_gap`, default `1 Mb`) — if the
  amplicon's *highest read-pair-support* junction reaches out to another
  **amplified region on the same chromosome** beyond the extent, the dominant
  rearrangement co-mobilises sequence outside the circle, so the call is
  downgraded to `status = "bridged"`. (Cross-chromosome translocations are the
  chimeric signature and are *not* downgraded.)

Every reported field (`bd_pe_support`, `bd_occupancy`, `bridge_partner`, …) is
documented in `?call_episomal_from_ampliconsuite`.

## Visualising the calls

`read_ampliconsuite()` output converts directly into `plot_sv_linear()` inputs. A
small helper turns the parsed graph into the `cnv_data` / `sv_data` the plotter
expects:

```{r aa-to-plot}
aa_to_plot <- function(graph, sample) {
  g <- read_ampliconsuite(graph)
  list(
    # AA graphs carry TOTAL copy number only (no allele-specific split), so we
    # supply `copyNumber` and let plot_sv_linear() draw total copy number.
    cnv_data = with(g$segments, data.frame(
      sample = sample, seqnames = chr, start = start, end = end,
      copyNumber = cn, ploidy = 2)),
    sv_data = with(g$junctions, data.frame(
      sample = sample,
      chrom1 = cA, start1 = pA, strand1 = sA,
      chrom2 = cB, start2 = pB, strand2 = sB,
      svclass = svclass, VF = pe_support, JCN = jcn)))
}
```

Because AA reports only total copy number, `plot_sv_linear()` draws a single
copy-number line and labels the axis *Copy number* (it does not assume the minor
allele is zero).

**GBM39 (episomal)** — the amplified EGFR segment bounded by a single
duplication junction (the boundary DUP): a clean simple-excision circle.

```{r plot-gbm39}
gbm39_pl <- aa_to_plot(gbm39_graph, "GBM39")
plot_sv_linear(
  sample   = "GBM39",
  cnv_data = gbm39_pl$cnv_data,
  sv_data  = gbm39_pl$sv_data,
  chromosome       = "chr7",
  chromosome_range = matrix(c(54.5e6, 56.3e6), nrow = 1)
)
```

**COLO320DM (complex)** — the MYC amplicon is a tangle of duplications,
inversions and translocations (it even co-amplifies segments on other
chromosomes), with no single DUP bracketing the extent: not a simple-excision
circle.

```{r plot-colo}
colo_pl <- aa_to_plot(colo_graph, "COLO320DM")
plot_sv_linear(
  sample   = "COLO320DM",
  cnv_data = colo_pl$cnv_data,
  sv_data  = colo_pl$sv_data,
  chromosome       = "chr8",
  chromosome_range = matrix(c(126e6, 130e6), nrow = 1)
)
```

## Bare AA runs (no AmpliconClassifier)

For an AA run without AC, take the extent from the reconstructed cycle:
`aa_cycle_intervals()` reads the dominant (highest-copy) cycle's segments from a
`*_cycles.txt` (dropping the AA source vertex, segment `0`). You can pass the
`*_cycles.txt` path straight to `intervals` — the caller detects it:

```r
call_episomal_from_ampliconsuite(
  graph_file = "SAMPLE_amplicon1_graph.txt",
  intervals  = "SAMPLE_amplicon1_cycles.txt")   # extent from the dominant cycle
```

## Using your own data

Point the two arguments at the matching files from an AmpliconSuite run or an
AmpliconRepository download:

```r
call_episomal_from_ampliconsuite(
  graph_file = "SAMPLE_amplicon1_graph.txt",
  intervals  = "SAMPLE_amplicon1_ecDNA_1_intervals.bed")
```

Chromosome names may carry a `chr` prefix or not, as long as the graph and the
BED agree. One AC amplicon can yield several ecDNA features (`ecDNA_1`,
`ecDNA_2`, …); classify each by passing its own interval BED with the shared
`*_amplicon<N>_graph.txt`. Breakpoint homology is often absent from AA graphs
(the field is written `None`), so for a homology signature use the PURPLE-native
`call_simple_excision()` path instead.
